svg.title: From layout edges to neighbour slots
svg.desc: Animated: PoseGraph classifies each edge of node 8 for pose (8, 90) by the bearing of the edge relative to the yaw: 31 LEFT, 9 RIGHT, 4 BACK, 13 FORWARD, each within 0.1 rad. Then three hypothetical edits: a diagonal edge that throws, a disallowed_edge_orientation that removes heading 90 and -90 from edge 8-13, and a 0.1 m misalignment that PoseGraph accepts but GetMotionType rejects.
svg.metadata: ["Pose (8, 90): W8 at heading 90. PoseGraph measures each edge against yaw = 90 x pi/180 = pi/2 rad in the atan2 frame (0 = +x, counter-clockwise), which points to +y. The four wedges are the translation slots: FORWARD at relative bearing 0, LEFT at +pi/2, BACK at pi, RIGHT at -pi/2, each +-0.1 rad (5.7 deg) wide. The yaw used as a math angle points out of the AGV's right side; the AGV faces -x, so LEFT is the facing direction: LEFT and RIGHT are locomotes, FORWARD and BACK strafes. All eight slots start at -1 (kInvalidIndex).", "Neighbour 31 (28.0253, 12.7753) also allows heading 90, so pose (31, 90) exists. dx = -2.857, dy = 0: bearing atan2(0, -2.857) = 180 deg; relative to the yaw: +90 deg, inside the LEFT wedge. Slot LEFT (3) = (31, 90): a locomote toward the approach of bay 7.", "Neighbour 9 (37.1856, 12.7753): dx = +6.3033, dy = 0, bearing 0 deg, relative -90 deg: RIGHT (1) = (9, 90), the other locomote direction.", "Neighbour 4 (30.8823, 10.4893): dx = 0, dy = -2.286, bearing -90 deg, relative -180 deg, the same angle as +180: BACK (2) = (4, 90), a strafe.", "Neighbour 13 (30.8823, 17.1663): dy = +4.391, bearing +90 deg, relative 0: FORWARD (0) = (13, 90), a strafe. Node 8 has rotation_allowed, so ROT_RIGHT (4) = (8, 0) and ROT_LEFT (5) = (8, 180), the nearest headings clockwise and counter-clockwise; no VRC, so slots 6 and 7 stay -1. Pose (8, -90) gets the mirror image: FORWARD 4, RIGHT 31, BACK 13, LEFT 9.", "Hypothetical edge 8-5 (not in the YAML). Both nodes allow heading 90, so the edge is classified: bearing atan2(-2.286, 6.3033) = -19.9 deg, relative -109.9 deg, 19.9 deg (0.35 rad) from RIGHT and outside every wedge. The PoseGraph constructor throws. Poses are built in node-id order, so pose (5, -90) gets there first and the message reads \"Edge 5 <-> 8 with invalid translation connection!\". Had the nodes shared no heading, the edge would be skipped without a word.", "Hypothetical disallowed_edge_orientation: 90 on edge 8-13. IsAngleOrReciprocal(90, heading) is true for 90 and -90, so (8, 90) loses FORWARD, (8, -90) loses BACK, and 13's poses lose 8. Node 13 has only those two headings, so the edge is gone from the PoseGraph while Layout::HasEdge(8, 13) stays true. 8-13 is the only edge between the two YAML sandboxes, so the pose graph would split in two.", "Hypothetical: node 31 moved 0.1 m north (y = 12.8753). Bearing 178.0 deg, relative +88.0 deg: still inside the 5.7 deg LEFT wedge, so PoseGraph builds the edge. GetMotionType checks the same edge with IsLocomoteOrStrafe at 1e-3 rad: 2.0 deg (0.035 rad) is neither a locomote nor a strafe, and it throws \"Edge traversal is not perpendicular to where we are.\" on the first command that uses it.", "The complete picture: the four Pecos edges of node 8 fill slots 0 to 3 of (8, 90), rotation fills 4 and 5. Three rules to remember when editing edges: an off-axis edge throws only when the two nodes share a heading; a disallowed orientation removes a heading and its reciprocal from one edge; and PoseGraph's 0.1 rad tolerance is 100 times looser than the 1e-3 rad of GetMotionType."]

g.text: The YAML edges are undirected and carry no direction names. PoseGraph gives them names per pose: it takes the atan2 bearing of each edge, subtracts the pose's yaw and snaps the result to one of four slots, within 0.1 rad. Step through the four

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: neighbours of pose (8, 90), then three hypothetical edits that throw, remove an edge, or pass here and fail later.
